business_rules.statement: There are exactly three named platform access classes and only three: the normal support session, the compliance-emergency path, and the JBS access grant. No ambient browsing exists anywhere on the console.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Super Admin platform console access layer
business_rules.applies_to: All platform-side access into tenant record-level content

business_rules.statement: The audit log is one append-only log per tenant under the one-transaction guarantee; an action that cannot be audited does not happen.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Transactional commit — audit event commits in the same transaction as the action
business_rules.applies_to: Every consequential action on the platform

business_rules.statement: No role, tenant-side or platform-side, can modify or delete an audit entry. The edit and delete controls do not exist, because the log is append-only and immutable for every role.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Audit log storage and UI (control does not exist)

business_rules.statement: A support session is read-only, reason-required, ticket-linked, with a default two-hour time box, a tenant-visible banner with an End-session control the tenant can exercise, and mirroring into the tenant's audit stream.
business_rules.applies_to: Support (platform) role sessions into a tenant

business_rules.statement: The support-session banner text is specific and fixed: "Platform support is viewing your tenant. Started [time]. Engineer [name]. End session [button]".
business_rules.applies_to: Tenant Admin during an active support session

business_rules.statement: No banner means no session: the session does not open, or terminates, if the banner cannot be shown — visibility is a precondition of the access rather than a decoration on it.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Banner heartbeat tied to the session

business_rules.statement: The compliance-emergency path requires two authorisations — the root and one Admin — is time-boxed, with the scope declared before it opens; it is the only path with write capability into tenant data and the only entry into a compliance-suspended tenant.
business_rules.enforcement_point: PER-SA-EMERGENCY-AUTHORISE, scope enforcement at object access
business_rules.applies_to: Platform-side write access into tenant data

business_rules.statement: Access outside the declared emergency scope is refused and recorded, not merely logged as a warning; widening requires a new request with new authorisations, never an in-session widening.
The tenant automatically receives a post-session report after a compliance-emergency session; the control to suppress the tenant report does not exist.
No End-session control is offered for the compliance-emergency class, because an emergency access the tenant could terminate would not be an emergency access.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Delivery Operations Hub banner for emergency class

business_rules.statement: Suspension is a three-state machine drawn by data type: writes that grow or reshape the account's master data are blocked first while writes that operate the existing account continue as long as possible.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Delivery Operations Hub enforcement layer working from enumerated lists

business_rules.statement: Soft suspension blocks creation of new Jobs, Workers, locations, shifts, parts, and all configuration edits, while recertification of existing workers deliberately stays open.

Hard suspension is read-only except the enumerated completion pipeline: no new runs, while in-flight runs complete, capture, sync, compute summaries and close, with mandatory notifications and audit continuing.
Compliance suspension blocks all logins immediately, stops in-flight runs, and locks devices at next contact with the fixed worker-facing message.
The worker-facing compliance message is fixed and verbatim: "Operation suspended. Contact your supervisor. Your work has been saved."
A device locks only at next contact, preserving all local data; unreached devices are enumerated individually with their last-seen times and no claim of enforcement is made for them.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Command channel and Super Admin device enforcement list

business_rules.statement: Maker-checker is absolute on the console: a Platform Engineer's change is submitted and takes effect only when an Admin approves it; user creation and role changes are root-only.
business_rules.applies_to: All Super Admin platform console changes

business_rules.statement: The critical class — tier publication, compliance suspension, all-tenant broadcast, device wipe and de-authorisation, emergency pause and resume separately, erasure and archival execution, retention-value changes, legal-hold place and release, severity-catalog changes and floor-register changes — is approved by the root.

The evaluation gate is hard, always, for every tenant, and binds every operator of the platform console including its root account: no agent, capability, or composed behaviour goes live without passing its evaluation scenarios.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Evaluation harness; the enablement control is not offered at all while a scenario fails
business_rules.applies_to: Every atom, agent and composed behaviour

business_rules.statement: Six ENFORCED invariants render locked with no off position for any account including the root: the evaluation gate, sandbox-before-publish, encryption at rest, encryption in transit, cross-tenant analytics anonymisation, and the one-transaction audit guarantee.
business_rules.applies_to: Every console account including the root

business_rules.statement: Emergency pause never suppresses the on-device deterministic layer: gates, specification checks, severity classification and the Severity 1 hold continue untouched, and the deterministic backbone has no off switch.

In-flight agent runs checkpoint at their next stage boundary and park; raised gates stay human-decidable; resume is a separate audited act; the pause renders as agent unavailability and never as silence.

A failing evaluation cannot be enabled by any account; if the scenarios themselves are wrong, changing the scenarios is itself a submitted change requiring approval, so the gate cannot be weakened by quietly editing its own test.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Evaluation harness plus maker-checker on scenario changes

business_rules.statement: Versioning is semantic: a patch carries no operating-behaviour change and applies directly while being tracked; minor and major are the notified classes where the Job Owner decides adoption and a mandatory republish description doubles as the worker-facing change notice.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Studio release classification and Delivery Operations Hub adoption decision

business_rules.statement: In-flight runs are never re-based; scheduled-not-started runs get an explicit rebase-or-keep choice; completed runs are immutable.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Version pinning on the run's work package

business_rules.statement: The change notice appears on the first screen of the next execution, drawn from the mandatory republish description, and altered steps are flagged in situ; the notice is part of starting the work rather than an inbox item that can be ignored.
business_rules.applies_to: Worker starting an execution on a newly adopted notified-class version

business_rules.statement: Nothing is purged: the tenant-set retention value is a hot-retrievability horizon, default 15 years, and beyond it data tiers to lower-cost storage and remains retrievable.
Worker personal data anonymises at 24 months after archival for standard commercial tenants and never in Regulated-Industry mode; anonymisation is the platform's one irreversible act.
Export on archival is provided at no charge and archival does not execute until it has been provided.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Archival execution screen — Skip the export is disabled

business_rules.statement: A legal hold in force suspends tiering and any compliance-driven deletion for its scope; legal-hold place and release are critical-class, root-approved actions.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Data lifecycle service and approval validation

business_rules.statement: The platform is provisioned with exactly one Super Admin account, created through the backend at platform commissioning and never through any user interface; it is the only account that can create other accounts.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Singleton constraint at backend provisioning; the console has no create path for it

business_rules.statement: Tenants may make the platform stricter than default and may never make it looser than the floor; the floor register rejects rather than logs an out-of-bound value at the point of entry with the bound stated.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Super Admin tenant-configuration registry at point of entry

business_rules.statement: Atoms arrive only by backend migration; the console has no create flow for atoms by design.
Onboarding is invitation-driven; there is no public self-signup at version 1 and pilots are invitation-only with no public free trial.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Super Admin platform console tenant list — Create is an Admin action

business_rules.statement: A pilot tenant is functionally identical to a paying tenant — same platform, same gates, same isolation — and conversion preserves the tenant identifier with zero re-onboarding.
There is no payment integration, no invoicing, and no pricing engine at any tier; tier records carry no price metadata.
A per-tenant override is stored as a flag on the tenant record — visible and audited — and never as an edit to the tier record.
Cross-tenant data isolation is platform-fixed for everyone always and memory isolation is absolute — nothing is shared with another tenant and nothing is used as external training data.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Isolation assertion before tenant status becomes active

business_rules.statement: A tenant workspace never exists without an open tenant audit log; a workspace without a log is never allowed to exist, not even briefly.
Exactly one Tenant Admin account is seeded by the console and no further tenant user can be created from the console; thereafter user management is tenant-administered in the Delivery Operations Hub.
A locale pack with untranslated keys fails publication rather than installing with gaps.
There are five fixed tenant roles at version 1 and custom roles are deferred; multi-role is additive and the audit log records the user identity and the action, never an acting-as-role fiction.
At least one Tenant Admin always exists, and an approver role must exist whenever a Job exists.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Mandatory-role check at the Job-creation path and at Tenant Admin removal

business_rules.statement: Qualifications are supervisor-entered with a full audit trail; self-attestation is not permitted, and no worker may record their own qualification.
At expiry under the strict posture, re-assignment to runs requiring the expired certification is blocked, the worker may complete the entire current run, and there is no grace period beyond it.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Qualification gate on the device at step level

business_rules.statement: The four qualification warning stages at 14, 7, 1 and 0 days cannot be removed or delayed; tenants may add earlier warnings only.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Platform floor held on the Super Admin platform console; tenant widening rejected

business_rules.statement: A schedule can never be the enforcement mechanism; a missed qualification warning never suppresses the qualification block itself and a missed run-finish tick leaves the run complete and never finishes it early.
Area split, merge and re-parent are not supported at version 1; a structural re-parent is blocked while in-flight Jobs exist and archive-and-recreate is the sanctioned path.

The mandatory notification baseline — subscription and tier lifecycle events, qualification-expiry warnings at 14, 7, 1 and 0 days, and allocation-ladder events including burst entry — cannot be disabled, and in-app notifications cannot be muted.
Closing a Site or Area is a soft archive that cascades: every bound Job auto-pauses, the Tenant Admin is notified with the list, and reassignment is prompted before archival completes.

Every worker has their own platform identity and login; the credential is the person's, never the device's. There is no cap on concurrent workers per run, and step attribution is always by individual identity, never by device.
business_rules.applies_to: Workers on the Frontline Worker Application

business_rules.statement: Where this chapter and a catalog chapter appear to differ, the catalog chapter governs the detail and this chapter governs the sequence.

contradictions.description: Soft-suspension exit trigger: §4.2.4 says an operator signal in Super Admin with no payment integration; §8.9.2 and Part IX say Automatic on payment / soft clears on payment.
conflicting_values: release by an explicit operator signal in the Super Admin platform console

contradictions.description: Atom/feature enablement authority: §8.2.2 makes it a Platform Engineer change requiring Admin approval; §8.19 makes platform-side tenant current-value changes including feature enablement an Admin action.
conflicting_values: Platform Engineer change requiring Admin approval

contradictions.description: Record-finish window bounds are stated as settled in §4.6.8 and §8.19 and as an open drafting value in §2.4; this chapter preserves both readings and does not choose.
conflicting_values: settled: default 48 hours within 24 hours to 7 days

contradictions.description: Site level: §2.1 marks Site-as-required-minimum as an open drafting recommendation while §4.3.1 states it as mandatory.
conflicting_values: mandatory anchor for timezone and shifts

contradictions.description: Job anchoring: §2.1 says one parent node per Job at the configured depth; §4.5.1 states one Area per Job as a hard constraint.
conflicting_values: one parent node per Job at the configured depth
one Area per Job as a hard constraint

contradictions.description: Authoring grants are layered on Supervisor or Quality Manager (§5.18) while the source elsewhere lists Plant Manager in a table headed Fixed role.
conflicting_values: authoring grant layered on Supervisor or Quality Manager
Plant Manager listed as a Fixed role

contradictions.description: Wipe on an unreachable device: §7.11 and §8.13.3 require a final sync attempt before erasure, which an offline device cannot perform; the source does not state how long a wipe command may remain pending.
conflicting_values: final sync attempt required before erasure
an offline device cannot perform a final sync

contradictions.description: Authority matrices use `Supervisor+` and `QM+` forms without defining an ordering across five additive roles.
conflicting_values: the five tenant roles are additive with no ordering

failures_fallbacks.trigger: An action that occurs without its audit event; audit store unavailable
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Transactional refusal of the action
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Affected write paths refuse rather than proceed, degrading the platform to read-only for audited operations
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: A platform that will not change anything it cannot record
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The audit store returning; reconciliation is a gap analysis over the refused operations, none of which occurred

failures_fallbacks.trigger: An incomplete chain — a decision whose audit entry cannot be found
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The one-transaction guarantee; where a gap appears, the gap is itself the finding
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Reconstruction from the object's own state history, a weaker but non-empty source
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: An honestly reported gap, never a reconstructed entry
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A platform-side fix; reconciliation is a documented comparison of object state histories against the log

failures_fallbacks.trigger: An export fails or exceeds limits
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: A narrower filter
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: A scoped platform-side extract, itself an access event appearing in Platform Access History
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: An auditor with a partial but honestly bounded extract and a recorded request for more
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Not stated beyond the scoped extract; bulk export to tenant-owned storage is deferred beyond V1

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Client Command Center access attempted by the Read-only Auditor
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: None — there is no fallback that grants access, and none is wanted
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Not applicable
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The refusal is the control
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Not applicable

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The re-open question after a tenant terminates a session
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Recommendation: a fresh reason and ticket reference
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The tenant's control is nullified in practice
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Not resolved here
failures_fallbacks.recovery: In-app notification to the Tenant Admin on any re-open within the same day and a visible re-open count in Platform Access History — DEC-SUPPORT-001

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A banner that does not render, making an access invisible to the tenant
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The session does not open, or terminates, if the banner cannot be shown
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The engineer works from anonymised metadata and telemetry from the named administration layer
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No record-level access
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A working banner; reconciliation is Platform Access History showing the aborted session and its reason

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A support engineer attempting a write into tenant data
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: None — there is no fallback that grants write capability to a support session
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The only path with write capability is the dual-authorised compliance-emergency path
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: A support engineer who can describe the fix and cannot perform it
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Take the compliance-emergency path with two authorisations, a declared scope and an automatic report

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The second authorisation cannot be obtained — the root account holder is unreachable during an incident
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The remaining access classes: the read-only support session; the named administration and telemetry layer
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The tenant's own team acting inside their own workspace with their own roles
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No emergency session, preserving the dual-authorisation control
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Recommendation — R&D: a documented root-custody continuity procedure outside the platform

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Post-session report generation fails, or the emergency banner/time box
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The mirrored audit events remain in the tenant's own log and are queryable directly
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Not stated beyond the mirrored log
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: A tenant with full audit visibility and a missing summary document
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Regeneration of the report

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Writes inside the declared scope (credential revocation, legal hold)
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Not stated separately
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Not stated separately
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Not stated separately
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Not stated separately

failures_fallbacks.trigger: An attempt outside the declared emergency scope
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Refused and recorded rather than logged as a warning; the refusal appears in the tenant's report
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: A genuinely necessary object lies outside the declared scope
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: An incomplete emergency action and an honest report
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A new request with a new scope and a new pair of authorisations, not an in-session widening

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A suspension enforced inconsistently — blocked on the web and not on a device, or the reverse
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The enforcement architecture: Delivery Operations Hub is the system of record and the command channel is the delivery mechanism; an unreached device is shown as not yet reached
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Fleet action from the Super Admin platform console, which faces the same reachability limit (DEC-WIPE-001, DEC-SUSPDEV-001)
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Web surfaces fully constrained and unreached devices individually listed as unreached
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Device contact; reconciliation is the per-device enforcement list

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The soft-suspension exit trigger disagreement
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The adopted operator-signal reading under DEC-SUSP-001
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Under the superseded reading the platform would need a payment signal it has no integration to receive
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: A tenant that remains in soft suspension, operating normally, until a human clears it
failures_fallbacks.recovery: An explicit operator signal in the Super Admin platform console

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Over-blocking: a soft suspension that stops something the operational pipeline needs
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The enforcement layer works from the enumerated lists rather than a coarse read-only flag
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: A platform-side correction under the maker-checker cycle, with the floor genuinely stopped meanwhile
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The tenant being lifted out of soft suspension entirely rather than left half-blocked
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A corrected enforcement rule; reconciliation is a review of blocked-write events against the enumerated blocked set

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A completion pipeline that stalls — a device that never returns, or a run that cannot reach complete
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The supervisor's manual close on the Delivery Operations Hub run record, an audited act with a mandatory note
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The finish window still guarantees the run finishes even if the device never returns; the record closes with its gap documented
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: A closed record that honestly states what is missing
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Device return within the finish window folds late captures in flagged as late arrival; after finish the audited-recompute rule applies

failures_fallbacks.trigger: An action that could plausibly belong either to hard suspension or the completion pipeline (e.g. reassigning a run)
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The source resolves it: substitution remains available where needed to complete an in-flight run
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: For any genuinely ambiguous action, refusal with a reason
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: A slightly over-constrained tenant rather than an under-constrained one
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Not stated

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A compliance suspension applied without root approval
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The critical-class rule makes it impossible: the submission does not take effect
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Not applicable
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: A pending submission and an unchanged tenant
failures_fallbacks.recovery: There is deliberately no emergency path that bypasses the root approval for this action

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A device does not receive the lock command
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The pull-based command channel delivering at next contact whenever that occurs
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: No further technical fallback — the device is listed as unreached with its last-seen time and named in the tenant's post-review report
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: A locked fleet minus an explicitly enumerated set of unreached devices, never a claim of complete enforcement
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Device contact, or physical recovery by the tenant's own security process; reconciliation is the per-device enforcement list against the fleet inventory

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Reading the per-device enforcement list where devices are unreached
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Rendered from per-device command state with no claim of full enforcement
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Governed by DEC-SUSPDEV-001 and DEC-WIPE-001
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Honest per-device state
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Device contact

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A console change that takes effect without its approval; approval service unavailable
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Refusal — the change is submitted and does not apply until approved
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Engineering-class changes queue as submitted and nothing applies
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: A platform running on its last approved configuration with a visible queue of unapplied changes
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The approval service returning; reconciliation is the change queue and its audit trail

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Disablement, deprecation or rollback of a deployed capability — not described by the source
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Recommendation — R&D: disablement follows the same maker-checker path as enablement
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: In-flight agent runs depending on the capability checkpoint and park exactly as under an emergency pause
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No tenant-visible behaviour changes without the tenant's own version and adoption machinery where package-borne values are affected
failures_fallbacks.recovery: DEC-AGENTLC-001 — not resolved here

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A capability that fails its evaluation scenarios
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: There is no fallback that enables it; correction and re-evaluation is the first and only path
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: If the scenarios themselves are wrong, changing them is itself a submitted change requiring approval
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: A registered, disabled capability with its failure evidence attached
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A passing run; reconciliation is the atom's evaluation history, which retains the failing runs permanently

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Emergency pause and resume actions
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Not stated separately
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Not stated separately
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Not stated separately
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Resume as a separate audited act

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A pause that renders as silence with no explanation
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The explicit unavailability statement on the agent activity panel
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The agent health flag, which flags a failure immediately in plain terms and notes that platform operations has been notified

failures_fallbacks.recovery: Resume; reconciliation is the agent activity log showing the paused interval

failures_fallbacks.trigger: An agent run interrupted mid-stage, which could leave a partial artifact

failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The run is abandoned and its partial output discarded rather than presented
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: A parked or abandoned agent run and a fully intact human decision queue
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Resume — parked agent runs continue from their checkpoints

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The risk that pausing agents weakens the safety layer
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: None needed — the layers are separate by construction; the deterministic backbone has no off switch
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Not applicable
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Not applicable
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Verification is the test rather than a fallback — TEST-30-28-002

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A version change reaching a worker mid-run

failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Not stated beyond the pin
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: A run completing on its original content with the new version staged and waiting

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Publication of a notified-class version
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Not stated separately
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Not stated separately
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Not stated separately
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Not stated separately

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A Job Owner who never decides adoption
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The Job continues on its current version indefinitely, which is safe and stale; the outstanding decision remains visible on the Job
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Where the Job Owner has left the organisation, Job Owner reassignment as a field edit conferring no permissions
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: A Job running known-good content with a visible undecided adoption item

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A change notice that cannot be rendered — a package staged without its notice text
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Refusal to start the execution on the new version, falling back to the previously adopted version
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The run does not start and the condition escalates
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No execution rather than an uninformed execution

failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Not stated separately
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Not stated separately

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A retrieval request that takes longer than the requester expected
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Retrievability is unconditional even where speed is unstated: the data exists and can be produced
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The retrieval expectation is an open drafting value of minutes, hours, or next business day

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Anonymisation

failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Switching a tenant into Regulated-Industry mode later does not and cannot restore already-anonymised identities
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: A complete quality record with severed identities — measurement, result and evidence survive and the person becomes an opaque worker identifier
failures_fallbacks.recovery: No recovery, by design; the first and only mitigation is the onboarding conversation — DEC-ANON-001

failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Not stated here
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Not stated here

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The one-transaction audit guarantee cannot be satisfied — the audit store is unavailable at the moment of root creation
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Retry the commissioning transaction against the audit store once it is healthy; commissioning is idempotent
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The audit store remains unavailable, or a partially created identity is detected
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The platform remains STATE-PLAT-UNCOMMISSIONED and unreachable
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Restore the audit store, verify no partial identity exists, and re-run commissioning; final authoritative state is the platform audit log

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The single sign-on provider is unavailable, so a newly created account cannot authenticate
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The account exists and waits; the root retains access through its own posture
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The identity provider remains unavailable long enough to block a needed Admin approval
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Pending changes stay pending; nothing applies silently and aging critical requests re-notify the root
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The identity provider is restored, the Admin authenticates, and the queue is worked in order

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The tier record required for this tenant is drafted but not published
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Assign the nearest published tier and record a per-tenant override flag on the tenant record
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: No published tier fits and the override would breach a floor
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The onboarding request stays qualified but unprovisioned; no data space is created
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The Admin drafts the tier version and the root publishes it as a critical-class action with its grandfathering treatment declared

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The isolated data space is provisioned but the tenant audit stream cannot be opened
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Retry the provisioning transaction as a whole
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The retry fails or a partially provisioned space is detected
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The tenant is not created, the request remains qualified, and no partial workspace is left addressable
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Clear partials, restore the audit store, re-provision

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The tenant identity provider is unreachable, so single sign-on cannot complete
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The platform-managed credential path
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The managed credential cannot be delivered because the email vendor is failing and the in-app inbox needs a session
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Bright Bikes has no live Tenant Admin, no configuration is possible, and no work can be created
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The client's platform team re-seeds or re-issues the first Tenant Admin credential as a console action

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The parts-registry bulk upload exceeds the platform's ingestion limits
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Split the upload into conformant batches and re-upload; parts may also be added inline during Studio authoring
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The file is malformed rather than merely large
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No partial registry is stored; the tenant is told which rows failed and why
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Correct the file and re-upload; final authoritative state is the Delivery Operations Hub parts registry

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The mandatory-role check finds no approver-capable role at the moment a Job is later created
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The Tenant Admin assigns the Quality Manager role to a second qualified person
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: No person is available to hold it
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No Job can leave draft, so no run can be scheduled and no work executed against an unapproved definition
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A Quality Manager account is created or the role is added; segregation of duties is re-checked at approval time

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The expiry schedule is armed with a wrong date because the certificate was mistyped
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The supervisor corrects the record, which recomputes all four occurrences from the corrected date rather than shifting them relatively
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The error is discovered after the certification has already expired and blocked an assignment
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The block stands — the gate is enforced on the device and never by the notification
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Correct the record, or grant a clearance as Client Command Center action ten with a mandatory categorised reason
